tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem.

Usage:
- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- If this is an existing file, you MUST use the Read tool first to read the file's contents. This tool will fail if you did not read the file first.
- Prefer the Edit tool for modifying existing files — it only sends the diff. Only use this tool to create new files or for complete rewrites.
- NEVER create documentation files (*.md) or README files unless explicitly requested by the User.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Prefer it to 'screenshot' to find what to tap (tap a frame's center), read text, or check a control's state or value; use 'screenshot' for layout, color, and images. Default: the whole visible tree; x/y: the element under that point with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container); marker: the first element whose label (or match_key) contains that text. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted, and text longer than its area shows is cut and ends with ... (occlusion and transparency are not detected); a tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with x/y or marker; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring. Omit for the whole tree, or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type).

input.command: cat scripts/hooks/pre-commit 2>&1
input.description: Read pre-commit hook script

content.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Pre-commit hook:
#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
#
# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
  # nvm (most common on macOS)
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

  # fnm
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi

  # volta
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
  fi

  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)

registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)

if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
  git add .claude/registry/
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
    || true)

  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
    if ! node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null; then
      echo ""
      echo "  ❌  sync:ai-rules:fix failed — derived AI config files may be stale or partially"
      echo "      written. Fix the error above, then re-stage and commit again."
      echo ""
      exit 1
    fi
    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
#     automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'

  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
  fi

  echo ""
  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
  echo ""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen
#    When any experiences/*.tsx file is staged, regenerate definitions.ts
#    and stage it automatically. Blocks the commit on codegen failure.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

experiences_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E 'overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/.*\.tsx$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$experiences_staged" ]; then
  echo "Studio Experiences component staged — regenerating definitions.ts..."

  REAL_EXPERIENCES="overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences"
  tmp_exp=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_exp"' EXIT

  # Populate temp dir with the staged version of each .tsx.
  # Files that are not staged are copied from the working tree so the generator
  # sees a complete set. definitions.ts is excluded — it is the output target.
  for f in "$REAL_EXPERIENCES"/*.tsx; do
    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    name=$(basename "$f")
    [[ "$name" == "definitions.ts" ]] && continue
    if echo "$experiences_staged" | grep -qF "$f"; then
      git show ":0:$f" > "$tmp_exp/$name"
    else
      cp "$f" "$tmp_exp/$name"
    fi
  done

  remaining_tsx=$(find "$tmp_exp" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.tsx' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')

  if [ "$remaining_tsx" -eq 0 ]; then
    # Every experiences/*.tsx component was deleted in this commit — nothing
    # left to register. generateDefinitions.mjs treats zero components as a
    # hard failure (the right call for its normal "did I forget @cf-register"
    # use case), so don't invoke it here; there's no stale definitions.ts to
    # regenerate, just one to drop if it's still on disk and not yet staged
    # for removal.
    if [ -f "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts" ] && ! echo "$staged" | grep -qF "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"; then
      git rm -q "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
    fi
    echo "  ⏭️   No experiences/*.tsx components remain — skipping codegen, no definitions.ts to generate."
  elif ! CF_EXPERIENCES_DIR="$tmp_exp" node scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Contentful codegen failed. Fix the errors above and try again."
    exit 1
  else
    cp "$tmp_exp/definitions.ts" "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
    git add "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
    echo "  ✓  definitions.ts updated and staged."
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Derived configuration file guard
#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

blocked_files=()

# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)

while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

  # Only check files in derived locations
  case "$file" in
    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac

  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue

  # Extract all source paths from the synced-from comment
  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2, ...] — ... -->
  synced_sources=$(echo "$synced_line" \
    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//')

  [[ -z "$synced_sources" ]] && continue

  # If ANY source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
  # update — the developer edited a .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
  # Skip it.
  staged_names=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
  any_source_staged=false
  while IFS= read -r src; do
    src=$(echo "$src" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
    [[ -z "$src" ]] && continue
    if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qxF -- "$src"; then
      any_source_staged=true
      break
    fi
  done <<< "$(echo "$synced_sources" | tr ',' '\n')"
  if $any_source_staged; then
    continue
  fi

  # Fall back to the same AI-sources trigger condition step 1b uses to decide
  # whether to regenerate this file in the first place. A derived file's own
  # synced-from header may not yet list every source that legitimately feeds
  # it (e.g. a skill file added after the header was last written) — if step
  # 1b would have regenerated this file because a .claude/rules/*.md or
  # .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md file is staged, that is also a legitimate sync,
  # not a direct edit.
  if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qE '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$'; then
    continue
  fi

  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
  blocked_files+=("$file")

done <<< "$modified_staged"

if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
  echo ""
  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
    echo "       $bf"
  done
  echo ""
  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
  echo ""
  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
  echo ""
  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
  secret_violations=()

  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a JWT
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value matches a known provider secret format)")
      continue
    fi

  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)

  if [ "${#secret_violations[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
    echo ""
    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
      echo "    $v"
    done
    echo ""
    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
    echo ""
    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Scoped Vitest — run only the tests related to what's actually staged,

#!/bin/bash
# Pre-commit hook:
#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
#
# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
  # nvm (most common on macOS)
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

  # fnm
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi

  # volta
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
  fi

  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)

registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)

if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
  git add .claude/registry/
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
    || true)

  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
    if ! node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null; then
      echo ""
      echo "  ❌  sync:ai-rules:fix failed — derived AI config files may be stale or partially"
      echo "      written. Fix the error above, then re-stage and commit again."
      echo ""
      exit 1
    fi
    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
#     automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'

  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
  fi

  echo ""
  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
  echo ""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen
#    When any experiences/*.tsx file is staged, regenerate definitions.ts
#    and stage it automatically. Blocks the commit on codegen failure.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

experiences_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E 'overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/.*\.tsx$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$experiences_staged" ]; then
  echo "Studio Experiences component staged — regenerating definitions.ts..."

  REAL_EXPERIENCES="overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences"
  tmp_exp=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_exp"' EXIT

  # Populate temp dir with the staged version of each .tsx.
  # Files that are not staged are copied from the working tree so the generator
  # sees a complete set. definitions.ts is excluded — it is the output target.
  for f in "$REAL_EXPERIENCES"/*.tsx; do
    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    name=$(basename "$f")
    [[ "$name" == "definitions.ts" ]] && continue
    if echo "$experiences_staged" | grep -qF "$f"; then
      git show ":0:$f" > "$tmp_exp/$name"
    else
      cp "$f" "$tmp_exp/$name"
    fi
  done

  remaining_tsx=$(find "$tmp_exp" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.tsx' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')

  if [ "$remaining_tsx" -eq 0 ]; then
    # Every experiences/*.tsx component was deleted in this commit — nothing
    # left to register. generateDefinitions.mjs treats zero components as a
    # hard failure (the right call for its normal "did I forget @cf-register"
    # use case), so don't invoke it here; there's no stale definitions.ts to
    # regenerate, just one to drop if it's still on disk and not yet staged
    # for removal.
    if [ -f "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts" ] && ! echo "$staged" | grep -qF "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"; then
      git rm -q "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
    fi
    echo "  ⏭️   No experiences/*.tsx components remain — skipping codegen, no definitions.ts to generate."
  elif ! CF_EXPERIENCES_DIR="$tmp_exp" node scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Contentful codegen failed. Fix the errors above and try again."
    exit 1
  else
    cp "$tmp_exp/definitions.ts" "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
    git add "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
    echo "  ✓  definitions.ts updated and staged."
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Derived configuration file guard
#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

blocked_files=()

# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)

while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

  # Only check files in derived locations
  case "$file" in
    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac

  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue

  # Extract all source paths from the synced-from comment
  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2, ...] — ... -->
  synced_sources=$(echo "$synced_line" \
    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//')

  [[ -z "$synced_sources" ]] && continue

  # If ANY source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
  # update — the developer edited a .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
  # Skip it.
  staged_names=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
  any_source_staged=false
  while IFS= read -r src; do
    src=$(echo "$src" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
    [[ -z "$src" ]] && continue
    if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qxF -- "$src"; then
      any_source_staged=true
      break
    fi
  done <<< "$(echo "$synced_sources" | tr ',' '\n')"
  if $any_source_staged; then
    continue
  fi

  # whether to regenerate this file in the first place. A derived file's own
  # synced-from header may not yet list every source that legitimately feeds
  # it (e.g. a skill file added after the header was last written) — if step
  # 1b would have regenerated this file because a .claude/rules/*.md or
  # .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md file is staged, that is also a legitimate sync,
  # not a direct edit.
  if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qE '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$'; then
    continue
  fi

  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
  blocked_files+=("$file")

done <<< "$modified_staged"

if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
  echo ""
  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
    echo "       $bf"
  done
  echo ""
  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
  echo ""
  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
  echo ""
  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
  secret_violations=()

  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a JWT
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value matches a known provider secret format)")
      continue
    fi

  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)

  if [ "${#secret_violations[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
    echo ""
    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
      echo "    $v"
    done
    echo ""
    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
    echo ""
    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Scoped Vitest — run only the tests related to what's actually staged,
#    not the whole suite. `vitest related` walks the module graph from the
#    given files and runs whatever test files transitively depend on them
#    (or, for a staged *.test.ts(x) itself, just that file). Confirmed
#    live (2026-08-26): `vitest related` defaults to watch mode and hangs
#    forever without --run — that flag is not optional here.
#    Blocks the commit on a real test failure; the full unscoped suite
#    still runs (and blocks the PR) in CI regardless of what this catches.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

vitest_files=()
while IFS= read -r f; do
  [[ -z "$f" ]] && continue
  vitest_files+=("$f")
done < <(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR | grep -E '^overrides/.*\.(ts|tsx)$' || true)

if [ "${#vitest_files[@]}" -gt 0 ] && command -v node &>/dev/null; then
  echo "Running Vitest for files related to your staged changes..."
  if ! npx vitest related --run "${vitest_files[@]}"; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — a related Vitest test failed."
    echo "      Fix the failure above, then re-stage and commit again."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
fi

exit 0

1:name: Deploy Preview
3:# Ephemeral per-branch MRT preview environments. On every push to a feature/fix
5:# builds, and deploys — giving devs/testers a live URL to review during PR without
6:# waiting for a merge to develop. Companion teardown workflow: teardown-preview.yml.
9:# rejected 2026-09-05): digital-sit.yml's SIT Gate needs its own ephemeral preview of
11:# a stale static SIT URL, but giving it that via this *separate* workflow would mean
16:# digital-sit.yml has its own self-contained deploy-preview job instead (same
17:# scripts/computeMrtPreviewSlug.mjs naming, so teardown-preview.yml's eligibility
18:# regex still covers it) — see that file's own comment.
43:  group: mrt-preview-${{ github.ref_name }}
51:  deploy-preview:
52:    name: Deploy Preview
55:    # `environment: dev`, which made GitHub log a real Deployment tagged
58:    # always an isolated pr-<slug> MRT preview, never the shared dev tier
59:    # (confirmed against real Deployment records, 2026-08-25). The binding
86:      - name: Compute MRT preview slug
91:          SLUG=$(node scripts/computeMrtPreviewSlug.mjs "$BRANCH_NAME")
120:          import base64, json, os, sys, time, urllib.request, urllib.error
132:              req = urllib.request.Request(base + f'target/{SLUG}/', headers=headers)
135:                      return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30).read())
136:                  except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
144:                  except urllib.error.URLError as e:
168:              req = urllib.request.Request(
172:                  resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
174:              except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
186:                  req = urllib.request.Request(
190:                      urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
191:                  except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
205:          import base64, json, os, sys, time, urllib.request, urllib.error
211:          url = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/target/{SLUG}/'
217:              req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers)
219:                  body = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30).read())
220:              except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
244:              except urllib.error.URLError as e:
257:                  # URL in the PR comment if it ever did.
317:          # Always dev — ephemeral preview branches have no GitHub Environment of
331:              import urllib.parse
332:              safe_name = urllib.parse.quote(env_name, safe='')
362:      - name: Sync env vars to the preview target
369:          import base64, json, os, sys, urllib.request, urllib.error
401:          url   = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/target/{TARGET}/env-var/'
402:          req   = urllib.request.Request(
403:              url,
412:              resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
415:          except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
418:          except urllib.error.URLError as e:
425:      - name: Build and push to preview target
437:      # BrowserStack at the resulting URL instead of the static test-tier
444:      - name: Persist preview hostname for e2e-browserstack
446:          PREVIEW_HOSTNAME: ${{ steps.wait.outputs.hostname }}
447:        run: printf '%s\n' "$PREVIEW_HOSTNAME" > preview-hostname.txt
449:      - name: Upload preview hostname artifact
452:          name: mrt-preview-hostname
453:          path: preview-hostname.txt
465:      # Upserts on an exact HTML-comment marker (not a text substring) so a
466:      # coincidental match in someone else's comment can't be mistaken for ours,
467:      # and so redeploys update the same comment instead of spamming the thread —
468:      # the URL is deterministic from the slug and never changes between pushes.
469:      # Pattern mirrors protected-file-guard.yml's Tier 2 warning comment.
470:      - name: Post or update preview URL comment

53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:5:Measmerize is the third-party sizing widget on the PDP. It powers two surfaces:
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:8:2. **Size guide overlay** — opens as a slide-out without navigating away from the PDP (PRD-053, confirmed — size guide is a Measmerize overlay).
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:10:The PWA's job is narrow: inject the Measmerize script on PDP, place the required DOM containers, detect whether Measmerize has data for the current product, and fall back to the Contentful-managed size guide if it does not.
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:15:- Placing DOM containers (`#measmerize-modal`, `#measmerize-recommendation`)
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:18:- Rendering the Contentful size guide as a fallback when Measmerize has no data for the product
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:23:- Widget configuration in the Measmerize console (Zimmermann and Measmerize own this)
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:24:- Size guide content — Measmerize owns it where the widget has data; Contentful owns the fallback
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:25:- Measurement units toggle (cm / inches) — part of the Contentful fallback size guide (PRD-056), not the Measmerize widget
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:33:PWA injects Measmerize script tag once (deferred — after LCP image)
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:37:Measmerize initialises and checks its data store for this product
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:39:        ├── data exists → fires measmerize.widget.ready
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:42:        │   Measmerize mounts the widget in #measmerize-modal
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:43:        │   Customer clicks → Measmerize takes over and renders its overlay

53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:53:**Integration modes:** Measmerize supports two DOM integration patterns:
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:55:- **Standard** — place `<div id="measmerize-button">` on the PDP. Measmerize renders and manages its own "Find Your Size" button inside it. Use when no pre-existing size-guide modal exists.
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:56:- **Modal** — the PWA provides its own CTAs (e.g. separate "Find My Size" and "Size Guide" links). When the customer opens the overlay, the PWA calls `window.measmerize.modal.mount()`, which injects the widget into `<div id="measmerize-modal">`. No `#measmerize-button` div is needed.

Falls back to the Contentful size guide when Measmerize has no data for the product. **Consent approach unconfirmed — open item.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.

53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:1:# 17 — Measmerize (Find My Size / Size Guide)
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:5:Measmerize is the third-party sizing widget on the PDP. It powers two surfaces:
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:8:2. **Size guide overlay** — opens as a slide-out without navigating away from the PDP (PRD-053, confirmed — size guide is a Measmerize overlay).
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:10:The PWA's job is narrow: inject the Measmerize script on PDP, place the required DOM containers, detect whether Measmerize has data for the current product, and fall back to the Contentful-managed size guide if it does not.
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:15:- Placing DOM containers (`#measmerize-modal`, `#measmerize-recommendation`)
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:18:- Rendering the Contentful size guide as a fallback when Measmerize has no data for the product
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:23:- Widget configuration in the Measmerize console (Zimmermann and Measmerize own this)
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:24:- Size guide content — Measmerize owns it where the widget has data; Contentful owns the fallback
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:25:- Measurement units toggle (cm / inches) — part of the Contentful fallback size guide (PRD-056), not the Measmerize widget
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:33:PWA injects Measmerize script tag once (deferred — after LCP image)
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:37:Measmerize initialises and checks its data store for this product
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:39:        ├── data exists → fires measmerize.widget.ready
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:42:        │   Measmerize mounts the widget in #measmerize-modal
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:43:        │   Customer clicks → Measmerize takes over and renders its overlay
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:44:        │   Recommendation generated → fires measmerize.widget.recommend
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:47:        └── no data → fires measmerize.widget.unavailable
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:53:**Integration modes:** Measmerize supports two DOM integration patterns:
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:55:- **Standard** — place `<div id="measmerize-button">` on the PDP. Measmerize renders and manages its own "Find Your Size" button inside it. Use when no pre-existing size-guide modal exists.
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:56:- **Modal** — the PWA provides its own CTAs (e.g. separate "Find My Size" and "Size Guide" links). When the customer opens the overlay, the PWA calls `window.measmerize.modal.mount()`, which injects the widget into `<div id="measmerize-modal">`. No `#measmerize-button` div is needed.
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:58:Both surfaces (Find My Size and Size Guide) point to the same Measmerize widget.
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:60:**Confirmed 2026-07-06: Modal Integration is the required path.** The PWA owns the modal/slide-out shell (width, styling, tab switching between the Measmerize widget and the Contentful size guide fallback); Measmerize is inserted into it via `window.measmerize.modal.mount()`, which injects Measmerize's HTML directly into `<div id="measmerize-modal">` (not an iframe). The `#measmerize-button` div is not used.
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:67:window.measmerize.script.productCode = 'NEW_SKU';
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:72:**Modal re-mount:** If React re-renders the `#measmerize-modal` container, call `window.measmerize.modal.mount()` to restore the widget.
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:74:**SSR pre-check (optional):** To avoid a flash of the wrong UI on first paint, an unauthenticated REST check can determine at SSR time whether Measmerize has data for a product:
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:77:GET https://api.client.measmerize.com/integrations/v1/brands/{brandCode}/products/{productCode}
53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1:.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md:80:Returns `200` if Measmerize has the product, `404` if not.

content.content:
########## commit b73a3e2 diff for sizeGuideContent.tsx / renderMeasurementInstructions ##########
commit b73a3e2dd954fd82bf127e7328396d366782ea9f
Author: Jhoan Dela Cruz <jhoan.rose.dela.cruz@accenture.com>
Date:   Mon Sep 14 22:18:44 2026 +0800

    fix(sfcc-102): CR findings — locale canonicalisation, numeric validation, Contentful fetch gating
    
    - useSizeGuide: canonicalise SFCC hyphenated locale (en-AU) to Contentful
      underscore format (en_AU) before building localeKey and checking locales[],
      matching the sizeGuide key regex and locales validation list
    - useSizeGuide.test: fix Contentful fixture keys/locales[] to use underscore
      format; hook input stays hyphenated to assert canonicalisation
    - sizeGuideContent: reject partially-numeric strings (e.g. "17mm") in
      toDisplayRows — validate full string against /^\d+(?:\.\d+)?$/ before
      converting; parseFloat would silently parse "17mm" as 17
    - useContentful: add enabled flag to useContentfulEntries (default true, fully
      backwards-compatible); clears data, error, and isLoading when disabled
    - useSizeGuide: pass !!sizeGuideKey as enabled — products with no c_sizeGuide
      attribute no longer trigger a Contentful fetch for all sizeGuide entries
    - zimmTable: bordered variant borderLeft already applied (confirmed in diff)
    - sizeGuide.js: restrict RICH_TEXT_VALIDATIONS to paragraph nodes + bold/italic
      marks, aligned with renderMeasurementInstructions which only renders those
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

diff --git a/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.tsx b/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.tsx
index 913a9b7e..5bf697b3 100644
--- a/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.tsx
+++ b/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.tsx
@@ -32,9 +32,10 @@ export const toDisplayRows = (table: SizeGuideTable, unit: Unit) =>
       const str = String(v);
       const rangeMatch = str.match(/^(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*[–-]\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)$/);
       if (rangeMatch) return `${convertCm(parseFloat(rangeMatch[1]))}–${convertCm(parseFloat(rangeMatch[2]))}`;
-      const num = typeof v === 'number' ? v : parseFloat(str);
-      if (Number.isNaN(num)) return v;
-      return convertCm(num);
+      if (typeof v === 'number') return convertCm(v);
+      const trimmed = str.trim();
+      if (!/^\d+(?:\.\d+)?$/.test(trimmed)) return v;
+      return convertCm(Number(trimmed));
     }),
   }));
 
diff --git a/scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuide.js b/scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuide.js
index cca3e977..87693e0d 100644
--- a/scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuide.js
+++ b/scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuide.js
@@ -1,33 +1,15 @@
-// Standard RichText validations applied to all RichText fields in this content type.
-// Mirrors Contentful's default "restrict to common nodes/marks" preset.
+// RichText validations aligned with renderMeasurementInstructions in sizeGuideContent.tsx,
+// which renders paragraphs only and supports bold and italic marks. Restricting to this set
+// prevents content authors from using nodes (headings, lists, embeds, hyperlinks) or marks
+// (underline, code) that would be silently discarded at render time.
 const RICH_TEXT_VALIDATIONS = [
   {
-    enabledNodeTypes: [
-      'heading-1',
-      'heading-2',
-      'heading-3',
-      'heading-4',
-      'heading-5',
-      'heading-6',
-      'ordered-list',
-      'unordered-list',
-      'hr',
-      'blockquote',
-      'embedded-entry-block',
-      'embedded-asset-block',
-      'hyperlink',
-      'entry-hyperlink',
-      'asset-hyperlink',
-      'embedded-entry-inline',
-    ],
-    message:
-      'Only heading 1, heading 2, heading 3, heading 4, heading 5, heading 6, ordered list, ' +
-      'Unordered list, horizontal rule, quote, block entry, asset, link to Url, link to entry, ' +
-      'link to asset, and inline entry nodes are allowed',
+    enabledNodeTypes: [],
+    message: 'Only paragraph nodes are allowed',
   },
   {
-    enabledMarks: ['bold', 'italic', 'underline', 'code'],
-    message: 'Only bold, italic, underline, and code marks are allowed',
+    enabledMarks: ['bold', 'italic'],
+    message: 'Only bold and italic marks are allowed',
   },
 ];

content.text: Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/figma/2.2.111/skills/figma-design-to-code # Implement a Figma Design as Code (Design → Code) Use this skill to turn a Figma design into code in a target codebase. This is the **read-FROM-Figma** direction: pull design context out of Figma with `get_design_context`, then adapt it into the project's real stack. For the reverse direction — building or updating a design *in* Figma from code — use [figma-generate-design](../figma-generate-design/SKILL.md) instead. This skill owns the **workflow** for design-to-code. Parameter mechanics (nodeId / fileKey / branchKey extraction, URL parsing, `format`/`query` options, response shape) live on the `get_design_context` tool description itself — follow them there. **Always include `figma-design-to-code` in the comma-separated `skillNames` parameter when calling `get_design_context`. If this skill was loaded via an MCP resource, you MUST prefix the name with `resource:` (e.g. `resource:figma-design-to-code`).** This is a logging parameter used to track skill usage — it does not affect execution. ## Direction and Scope - You MUST use this skill for design → code: implementing, translating, or porting a Figma node into code. - You MUST NOT use this skill to write to Figma. ## Workflow ### 1. Call get_design_context first - You MUST call `get_design_context` on the target node before writing any code. It is your primary tool — a single call returns reference code, a screenshot, and contextual hints. - You MUST NOT reach for `get_metadata` or `get_screenshot` as a substitute. Use them only to orient (e.g. picking a node) or to validate, not in place of `get_design_context`. ### 2. Treat the output as a reference, not final code - The returned code is React + Tailwind enriched with hints. You MUST treat it as a REFERENCE, not as final code to paste verbatim. - You MUST adapt it to the target project's language, framework, component library, styling system, and conventions. Match the surrounding code. ### 3. Reuse what the project already has - Before writing new code, You MUST check the target project for existing components, layout patterns, and design tokens that match the design intent. - You MUST reuse the project's existing components and tokens instead of generating new equivalents from scratch. ### 4. Honor the response hints by priority Apply the hints in this order — earlier sources override later ones: 1. **Code Connect snippets** → use the mapped codebase component directly. 2. **Component documentation links** → follow them for usage and guidelines. 3. **Design annotations** → follow any designer notes or constraints. 4. **Design tokens (CSS variables)** → map them to the project's token system. 5. **Raw hex / absolute positioning** → loosely structured; lean on the screenshot for intent. ### 5. Reproduce images and icons faithfully Images and icons come back as `` elements whose `src` is a remote asset URL (`https://.../api/mcp/asset/...`). Apply these rules as you write the code: - **Render every icon/image from its exported asset.** Never hand-write or inline `` to fill it (`100%` or fixed px) — never `auto`, which blows the image up to its intrinsic size. ## Error Recovery - On a `get_design_context` error, STOP and read the message before retrying. - If the design URL has no `node-id` (a file-only URL), ask the user for a node-specific URL — You MUST NOT guess or pass an empty `nodeId`. - On a timeout, retry against a smaller node or selection. - You MUST NOT silently fall back to hand-writing the screen from the screenshot alone when `get_design_context` can still provide context.
