entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_design_context
entries.description:
Get design context for a Figma node — the primary tool for design-to-code workflows. Returns reference code, a screenshot, and contextual metadata that must be adapted to the target project. 

IMPORTANT: You MUST load figma-design-to-code guidance BEFORE calling this tool. Prefer the /figma-design-to-code skill if available; otherwise read the skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md MCP resource. 

NEVER call this tool without loading that guidance first — skipping it produces code that ignores the target project's existing components, design tokens, and conventions.

Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. If a URL is provided, extract the node id and file key from the URL, for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2` and the fileKey would be `:fileKey`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName then use the makeFileKey to identify the Figma Make file. Only for Figma Make files (URLs containing `/make/`), and only when calling get_design_context, assume the nodeId is `0:1`. The response will contain a code string and a JSON of download URLs for the assets referenced in the code. It will also include a screenshot of the node for context by default.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

clientLanguages.description: A comma separated list of programming languages used by the client in the current context in string form, e.g. `javascript`, `html,css,typescript`, etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which languages are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess.

clientFrameworks.description: A comma separated list of frameworks used by the client in the current context, e.g. `react`, `vue`, `django` etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which frameworks are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess

forceCode.description: Whether code should always be returned, instead of returning just metadata if the output size is too large. Only set this when the user directly requests to force the code.

disableCodeConnect.description: Whether Code Connect should be used to get the design context. Only set this when the user directly requests to disable Code Connect.

skillNames.description: A comma-separated list of Figma skill names being followed, if any (e.g. "figma-design-to-code", "figma-design-to-code,figma-code-connect"). Only pass this when explicitly instructed to by skill documentation. Used for logging purposes. If the skill was loaded via a skill-content MCP resource, prefix the skill name with "resource:". (e.g. "resource:figma-design-to-code", "resource:figma-design-to-code,resource:figma-code-connect")

excludeScreenshot.description: Whether to exclude the screenshot of the design from the response. IMPORTANT: it is not recommended to exclude screenshots. Only set this to true if the user has explicitly requested it or you are trying to preserve context.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_metadata
entries.description: IMPORTANT: Always prefer to use get_design_context tool. Get metadata for a node or page in the Figma desktop app in XML format. Useful only for getting an overview of the structure, it only includes node IDs, layer types, names, positions and sizes. You can call get_design_context on the node IDs contained in this response. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id, it can also be the page id (e.g. 0:1). IMPORTANT: This tool only works for Figma design files (URL path `/design/`). It is NOT supported for FigJam (`/board/`) or Slides (`/slides/`) files. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). The nodeId parameter is optional: when omitted, the tool returns a list of the top-level pages (guid + name) in the document instead of an XML dump — use this when you don't yet know which page or node to drill into. When the user has a current selection relevant to the request, the response is prepended with a "Currently selected nodes:" block listing the selection by guid and name, so you can tell whether it matches the queried nodeId. If the URL includes `node-id`, extract it and pass it as nodeId; for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, do not set nodeId; omit the field so the tool lists top-level pages. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_screenshot
entries.description: Generate a screenshot for a given node or the currently selected node in the Figma desktop app. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`). The optional `maxDimension` parameter (positive integer, max 65536, default 1024) caps the longer edge of the rendered PNG in pixels — increase it when you need to inspect fine detail, decrease it for thumbnails or to save context. The JSON metadata entry in the response includes both `width`/`height` (the rendered PNG size) and `original_width`/`original_height` (the node's natural canvas size before any clamping), so callers can decide whether to re-request at a higher `maxDimension`. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. nodeId parameter is REQUIRED. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. fileKey parameter is REQUIRED. If a URL is provided, extract the file key and node id from the URL. For example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/pqrs/ExampleFile?node-id=1-2 the extracted fileKey would be `pqrs` and the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). By default this tool returns a short-lived URL to the screenshot plus curl instructions for downloading the PNG — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding the image inline. The `enableBase64Response` parameter defaults to `false`. Only set `enableBase64Response: true` when the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests); when set, an inline base64 image entry is appended to the response in addition to the URL and curl instructions. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

contentsOnly.description: When true, renders the node in isolation — floating/overlapping content (e.g. connectors parented to the page that visually sit above a section) is excluded. Defaults to false so screenshots match what the user sees on the canvas. Only set to true if the caller specifically needs the isolated render.

enableBase64Response.description: When true, the response also includes the screenshot inline as a base64-encoded image entry, in addition to the short-lived URL and curl instructions. Defaults to false. Set to true ONLY if the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests)

maxDimension.description: Optional. Maximum pixel size of the longer edge of the rendered screenshot — the server scales the node so that max(width, height) ≤ maxDimension while preserving aspect ratio. Defaults to 1024. Must be a positive integer; values above 65536 are rejected. Increase when the agent will visually inspect fine detail; decrease for thumbnails or to save context.

input.prompt:
You are reviewing (not building) ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa PR #113 — "feat(sfcc-102): size guide PDP slide-out with Contentful integration", by JhoanDelaCruz. Base `develop` @ ece4fc5dba111f1634d756773cd72fc4e983c283, head @ 53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1 (branch `feature/SFCC-102_pdp-ui-slide-out-size-fit`). Ticket: Jira SFCC-102 "PDP – Slide Out - Size Guide" — a Contentful-driven fallback size-guide drawer on the PDP (cm/inch toggle, size-conversion/body-measurement/garment-measurement tables). Explicitly OUT of scope per the ticket's own text: the Measmerize-powered "Find My Size" widget (that's sibling ticket SFCC-101, separate, still in progress) — do not flag its absence.

Changed files (19): `.claude/registry/{components,hooks,pages}.md` (auto-generated, ignore), `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTable/{index.tsx,index.test.tsx,index.stories.tsx,zimmTable.css.ts}` (new atom), `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` (modified: added `enabled` param), `overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.{ts,test.ts}` (new hook), `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (modified: wires the new tab in), `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.{tsx,test.ts,stories.tsx}` (new component), `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` (modified: two new fields), `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (modified: registers the new recipe), `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts` (modified: new types), `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` + `scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuide.js` (new Contentful content-type schema).

I (the human reviewer, FED lead) have ALREADY personally verified the following directly from source — do NOT re-investigate these, take them as settled ground truth:
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean on both base and head. `npm test` is 1219/1219 passing on head (83 files), matches the PR's own CI bot comment. `audit:tokens` shows the same 3 unacknowledged violations on base AND head (all in files this PR never touches) — pre-existing baseline debt, not introduced here.
- `npm run lint` (`overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}`) has exactly 2 NEW prettier-only errors, both in the new file `sizeGuideContent.tsx` (lines 98 and 238, both auto-fixable multi-line-JSX/ternary collapses) — contradicts the PR's own checklist claim of "0 errors on branch-changed files." Everything else this PR touches is lint-clean.
- CodeRabbit's locale-canonicalisation finding (hyphen→underscore, `useSizeGuide.ts`), the "validate entries"/`isValidTable` row-shape finding, the vertical-divider-border finding (`zimmTable/index.tsx`), the Contentful over-fetch/`enabled`-gating finding, and the partially-numeric-string finding (`toDisplayRows`, e.g. "17mm") are all CONFIRMED FIXED correctly in the current head — I read the actual code.
- A REAL, currently-open regression I found: commit `b73a3e2` correctly narrowed `RICH_TEXT_VALIDATIONS` in `scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuide.js` to match what `renderMeasurementInstructions` in `sizeGuideContent.tsx` actually renders (paragraphs + bold/italic only) — CodeRabbit marked this "addressed". Two commits later, `eb7f32af` ("sync sizeGuide.js to Contentful dev") silently reverted that narrowing back to the original broad `enabledNodeTypes` (headings/lists/hr/blockquote/embeds/hyperlinks) and `enabledMarks: ['bold','italic','underline','code']`, with no comment or discussion acknowledging the regression, and CodeRabbit's subsequent reviews never re-flagged it. Confirmed still broad at head. This is real and current — an editor using a heading/list/link/underline/code mark in the "Measurement Instructions" field will have it silently vanish on the PDP.
- `useSizeGuide.ts` still discards `error` from `useContentfulEntries` entirely and returns only `{sizeGuide, isLoading}` — a Contentful fetch failure is indistinguishable from "no size guide configured," so it fails silently rather than surfacing an error state. CodeRabbit flagged this ("outside diff" comment) and it was never addressed.
- The PR's own body claims "removed `mm` from `defaultUnit` union in both `contentful.ts` and `sizeGuide.js`" — true for `contentful.ts`'s TS type, but FALSE for `sizeGuide.js`: the same `eb7f32af` commit re-added `mm` to the Contentful schema validation (to match the live Contentful dev environment), which CodeRabbit and the author explicitly discussed and CodeRabbit withdrew its concern about. But the PR's own "Test checklist" line "`defaultUnit` dropdown no longer shows `mm`" is now stale/wrong given that reversal.
- `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` is a Tier 2 (CODEOWNERS: UI-designer / tier-2-approvers) file this PR modifies (registers the new `ZimmTable` recipe — purely mechanical, 2 lines, no raw design values) — confirmed via CODEOWNERS and via the bot's own auto-posted "Tier 2 Protected Files Detected" PR comment. The PR's own "Changed files"/"Required actions" tables never mention this file at all, even though the author correctly disclosed the OTHER Tier 2 file in this PR (the Contentful schema). Process/disclosure gap, not a code defect.
- The PR is currently `mergeable: CONFLICTING` against develop — but the ONLY conflicts are in the three auto-generated `.claude/registry/*.md` files (timestamps + a few consumer counts that drifted since another PR merged to develop) — trivially resolved by rebasing and re-running `node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`. Not a real content conflict.
- I confirmed `onFindYourSizeClick`/`onSizeGuideClick` (passed from `product-detail/index.tsx` into the base `<ProductView>` override, which forwards to `ZimmSizeSelector`) are pre-existing prop plumbing from an earlier ticket (SFCC-92) — this PR correctly just supplies the handler; nothing to fix there. I also live-verified in the browser (real MRT preview) that the "Find your size" link opens the drawer to the "Size Guide" tab correctly, and the sizeFit text renders — though no product in that environment's test catalog has a full Contentful size-guide match, so I could NOT verify the actual table rendering, CM/INCH toggle, or mobile horizontal-scroll affordance live — only via source/Storybook file reading. Flag this as an open verification gap in your own report too.
- Locale IDs across all 8 storefronts are confirmed 2-part at most (en, en-US, en-CA, en-GB, fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE) — so the `.replace('-','_')` single (non-global) replace in `useSizeGuide.ts` is safe for the current locale set, not a latent bug.
- `zimmTable.css.ts`'s `MIN_COL_WIDTH = calc(var(--zimm-scale-4xl) + var(--zimm-scale-m))` computes to 64px+16px=80px, applied only on the `standard` variant. Jira comment (Kiera Rikard-Bell, 2026-09-07, on SFCC-102) says "Minimum width of 64px on cells." I have NOT resolved whether 80px is a deliberate padding-inclusive choice or a real deviation from the 64px spec — flag this as something needing Marcel's/the designer's call, don't just assert it's wrong.

What I need FROM YOU (angles I have not personally covered — please verify independently, don't just trust my summary above for anything outside it):
1. **Conventions & structure sweep** across all 16 non-registry changed files against `.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `typescript.md`, `components.md`: magic numbers, JSDoc coverage (exported hooks/shared components), naming, import hygiene (circular imports, `../../../..` depth, no internal node_modules paths), Australian spelling in new identifiers/comments, `any`/`as`/non-null-assertion usage without justifying comments (I noticed `product-detail/index.tsx`'s `useMultiSite() as {locale?: {id?: string; alias?: string}}` cast has no comment — confirm and decide if worth flagging), whether `ZimmTableProps`'s flat-optional-fields shape (one type serving 3 render variants via `labelless`/`bordered` booleans, with `columns` required but unused in 2 of 3 variants) should really be a discriminated union per typescript.md's own guidance — I think this is a legitimate but minor nitpick, sanity check it.
2. **Test coverage adequacy** (pr-test-analyzer angle) for `useSizeGuide.test.ts`, `sizeGuideContent.test.ts`, `zimmTable/index.test.tsx` — do they cover the real edge cases (malformed Contentful data shapes beyond what `isValidTable` catches, the three-priority locale resolution's actual priority ordering, both bordered/labelless/standard ZimmTable render branches, the CM/INCH independent-per-table toggle state)? Is anything load-bearing untested?
3. **Accessibility** — the size-guide drawer content: tables (are they using real `<table>`/`<th>`/`<td>` semantics — yes per source, but check scope attributes / header association for screen readers), the CM/INCH toggle (`role="group"` + `aria-pressed` — already present per source, verify it's correct and sufficient), any color-contrast or WCAG 2.2 AA concern in the new recipe. Check `.claude/rules/components.md`'s accessibility section.
4. **Contract fidelity / integration boundaries** — `useContentful.ts`'s `enabled` param addition: confirm it doesn't break any of its other existing callers (grep all consumers of `useContentfulEntries`). Confirm the Contentful schema file (`sizeGuide.js`) is internally consistent (field types, editorInterface entries matching fields, the `key` regex `^size-guide__[a-z0-9_]+(__[a-z]{2}_[A-Z]{2})?$` actually matching what `useSizeGuide.ts` constructs). Check `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js`'s diff (+4/-0) for what it actually changed and whether that's safe/correct.
5. **Security** — I already confirmed no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere in this PR's new code (the rich-text renderer builds React elements directly). Sanity-check that conclusion, and check for anything else (e.g., unsanitised use of the Contentful image URL, SSRF-ish string building in `fallbackImgBase`).

Report CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE findings with file:line, a one-line failure scenario, and severity. Don't re-report anything I've already listed as settled above unless you find my conclusion is actually wrong — in which case say so plainly and show your evidence.

Judge whether ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa PR #113 ("feat(sfcc-102): size guide PDP slide-out with Contentful integration", JhoanDelaCruz, base develop@ece4fc5dba111f1634d756773cd72fc4e983c283, head@53206528f998b870437cfa5cddf1245b4ee382b1) delivers exactly what Jira SFCC-102 asks for — neither less nor more. For products where Measmerize is not configured, the Find My Size will not appear. This story does not cover the Measmerize-powered size guide — see SFCC-101." Key Jira comments (paraphrased, I already read the full ticket): default unit depends on storefront long-term (AU/UK/EU/HK/ME default cm, US domestic/intl default inch) but that storefront-level rule is explicitly deferred to a different ticket, SFCC-674 — so a per-Contentful-entry `defaultUnit` field (this PR's actual mechanism) is a reasonable interim; mobile scrolls horizontally with a shadow hint and a documented 64px cell-minimum for decimal values; final tab label wording is "Size Guide" (not "Size & Fit"). SFCC-101 (sibling, same assignee, also In Progress) is the Measmerize "Find My Size" CTA — explicitly a separate ticket; its own AC3 says if SFCC-102 isn't built yet, Measmerize's own trigger should just return no result — confirming the two tickets are meant to ship independently/asynchronously and this PR does not need to implement any Measmerize-configured/not-configured branching.

Specifically judge:
- Does the PR implement all three table types the ticket/Figma calls for (size conversions, body measurements, garment measurements) with correct data flow from Contentful through to render? (I've verified the code paths exist and are tested — you verify they're actually complete and match what Figma specifies, not just present.)
- Anything the PR added that ISN'T needed for SFCC-102 — over-scoping, e.g. speculative props/variants on `ZimmTable` with no current caller, dead code paths.
- Anything load-bearing missing — re-check against the Jira description and comments yourself.
- The `mm`/`defaultUnit` handling: the PR body claims it removed `mm` from both `contentful.ts` and `sizeGuide.js`, but I found `sizeGuide.js` still permits `mm` (deliberately reverted in a later commit, to match the live Contentful dev environment, with a documented reason) while `contentful.ts`'s TS type genuinely dropped it. Is this an acceptable interim inconsistency (schema permits, app never surfaces it) or does it constitute a real scope gap against the ticket?
- Whether wiring only the "Size Guide" tab and leaving "Find My Size" untouched (still a pre-existing placeholder elsewhere) is correct scoping given the sibling-ticket split described above, or whether you find evidence it should have gone further.

Give me a verdict: under-scoped / correctly-scoped / over-scoped, with the specific evidence either way. Don't edit any code.

      "value": "Overview\n--------\n\nThis page documents the size guide configuration for Zimmermann's SFCC + Contentful implementation. Size guides are surfaced on the PDP via a slide-out overlay (see [SFCC-102](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-102)).\n\nThe correct Contentful entry is resolved by the PWA at runtime by combining two independently sourced inputs:\n\n1. `sizeGuide` — retrieved from the SFCC product record. This is a product attribute set in Business Manager (see [SFCC-312](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-312)). Examples: `Clothing`, `Kids`, `Shoes`.\n2. `locale` — derived from the **PWA storefront session** (i.e. which locale the user is currently browsing). This is *not* stored on the product. Examples: `en_AU`, `fr_FR`.\n\nThe PWA combines these two values to construct the Contentful lookup key and fetch the right size guide content.\n\nResolution Logic\n----------------\n\n| **State** | `sizeGuide` **source** | `locale` **source** | **Contentful lookup key** |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| As-Is (current) | SFCC product attribute | Storefront level - separate size guides enabled for US storefronts | `size-guide__{sizeGuide}` e.g. `size-guide__Clothing` |\n| To-Be (future) | SFCC product attribute | PWA storefront session locale -  We should have local size guides for US, France, EU, Italian, UK, etc. | `size-guide__{sizeGuide}__{locale}` → fallback to `size-guide__{sizeGuide}` if no locale entry exists |\n\n**Locale Fallback Rule (To-Be)**\n\nResolution order: **locale-specific entry → Clothing entry → no guide (hidden)**.\n\nIf no Contentful entry exists for the `sizeGuide + locale` combination, the PWA falls back to the Clothing entry for that guide type. This means all products continue to display a guide even before locale-specific content is authored.\n\nAs-Is: Clothing Size Guides + Few US specific ones\n--------------------------------------------------\n\nThe following are the confirmed allowed values for the `sizeGuide` product attribute in Business Manager.\n\n| **sizeGuide Value** | **Description** | **Contentful Entry Key (proposed)** |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Clothing: OP-4 | Default guide for womenswear / general apparel | `size-guide__clothing_op` |\n| Kids | Childrenswear sizing | `size-guide__kids` |\n| Shoes | Footwear sizing | `size-guide__shoes` |\n| Denim | Denim / jeans sizing | `size-guide__denim` |\n| Mens | Menswear sizing | `size-guide__mens` |\n| Onesize | One size fits all — no measurements, care info only | `size-guide__onesize` |\n| Jewellery | Ring sizes, chain lengths, bracelet sizing | `size-guide__jewellery` |\n| Belts | Belt sizing by waist measurement | `size-guide__belts` |\n| Gloves | Glove sizing by hand measurement | `size-guide__gloves` |\n| Clothing - US | US - defaulting to inches instead of cm | `size-guide__clothing__en_CA`  & `size-guide__clothing__en` |\n| Denim - US | US - defaulting to inches instead of cm | `size-guide__denim__en_CA`  &  `size-guide__denim__en` |\n| Mens - US | US - defaulting to inches instead of cm | `size-guide__mens__en_CA`  &  `size-guide__mens__en` |\n| Kids - US | US - defaulting to inches instead of cm | `size-guide__kids__en_CA`  &  `size-guide__kids__en` |\n\nTo-Be: More Localised Size Guides\n---------------------------------\n\nThe PWA will combine the `sizeGuide` product attribute with the **active storefront locale** (from the browsing session, not the product) to construct a locale-specific Contentful lookup key.\n\nKey pattern: `size-guide__{sizeGuide}__{locale}`\n\nThe example below is a reference implementation to validate end-to-end resolution:\n\n| **sizeGuide (from product)** | **Locale (from storefront session)** | **Description** | **Contentful Entry Key (proposed)** | **Status** |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Clothing | `fr_FR` | Displayed when a shopper browses the French storefront locale and the product has `sizeGuide = Clothing`. Uses EU/FR sizing conventions for general apparel (e.g. dresses). | `size-guide__clothing__fr_FR` | ⚠️ Example — content TBC with Zimmermann |\n\n**Open Items**\n\n* The `Clothing / fr_FR` entry is a placeholder to validate the resolution logic. Actual French sizing content (measurements, conversion tables) to be confirmed with Zimmermann / merchandising before the Contentful entry is authored.\n* In Contentful - can we handle size guide mapping to multiple locales? e.g. in the EU International Storefront we have the en\\_CH locale but we may want to have that storefront/locale follow the French sizing (tagged to locale fr\\_FR). So then ideally the content team have this “French size guide for Shoes” but then they can multi-select the applicable locales as fr\\_FR and en\\_CH?\n\nThis is a proposed size guide table from Ilaria, currently ticket on Tryzen’s backlog for current website. By having locale available as an attribute for size guide in Contentful, we can enable the content team to set up localized size guides like so:\n\n![image-20260804-035854.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att384434178/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Clothing 0P - 4\n-----------------------------------\n\nAgreed with Dani to for now remove the Alpha sizing rows (S/M, M/L, S, M, L, XS, S, M, L) for now from the Clothing table - the new designs simplify the table. The content team can set up different versions of the Clothing table once that structure has been defined.\n\n![image-20260804-015117.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att383156227/download)![image-20260804-015136.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att384073730/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Kids\n------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-014951.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att383123459/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Shoes\n-------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-014614.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att383385604/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Denim\n-------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-015427.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att384303105/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Mens\n------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-032007.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att383614989/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Onesize\n---------------------------\n\nPending with Dani - assigning onesize probably means we do not render a size guide.\n\nSize Guide Content: Jewellery\n-----------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-015624.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att383057957/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Belts\n-------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-015703.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att384368641/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Gloves\n--------------------------\n\n![image-20260901-013004.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att461504514/download)\n\nSize Guide Content: Hats\n------------------------\n\n![image-20260804-035814.png](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content/383057926/child/attachment/att383483908/download)\n\nRelated\n-------\n\n* [SFCC-312](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-312) — sizeGuide product attribute configuration in BM\n* [SFCC-102](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-102) — Size guide UI / slide-out overlay (PWA)\n* [SFCC-304](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-304) — Contentful content types epic\n* Product Attributes — full SFCC product attribute set",

## Verdict: CORRECTLY-SCOPED

The three table types are complete, correctly wired end-to-end, and nothing SFCC-102 asks for is missing. But there are two small, contained over-scope items and — more importantly — a documentation-accuracy problem in the PR body itself that Marcel should make the author fix before merge, not because the code is wrong, but because the paper trail is.

## The five things you asked me to check

**1. All three table types, correct Contentful→render data flow?** Yes, verified. `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts` defines `sizeConversionsTable` / `bodyMeasurementsTable` / `garmentMeasurementsTable` on `SizeGuideEntry`; `sizeGuideContent.tsx` reads all three off the same resolved entry, guards each independently through `isValidTable` (line ~ the `isValidTable` const), and renders each through the same `ConvertibleTableSection` → `ScrollableTable` → `toDisplayRows` → `ZimmTable` pipeline. `scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuide.js` defines matching `Object`-typed fields for all three. The per-table CM/INCH toggle is real independence, not shared state — each `ConvertibleTableSection` owns its own `useState<Unit>` (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:169`-ish), so three tables on one PDP genuinely toggle separately, matching the Jira comment and the PR's own claim. `defaultUnit` is read once per Contentful entry and fed identically into all three sections (`sizeGuideContent.tsx`'s `initialUnit` computed from `sizeGuide?.fields.defaultUnit`) — exactly the "interim per-entry field, not per-storefront" mechanism the ticket comments describe as acceptable pending SFCC-674.

**2. Anything added that SFCC-102 didn't ask for?** Two real, minor items:
- `ZimmTable`'s `bordered` prop is a speculative axis. The one production caller, `ScrollableTable` in `sizeGuideContent.tsx:187-188`, always does `labelless={table.labelless}` **and** `bordered={table.labelless}` — the two props never vary independently in real content. That means the "labelless-but-not-bordered" render branch (`zimmTable/index.tsx:121`, a full ~40-line branch with its own `describe('ZimmTable — labelless table', ...)` Vitest suite and its own `Labelless` Storybook story) can only ever be reached by a story or a test calling `ZimmTable` directly — never by anything a shopper or a Contentful editor can trigger through `SizeGuideContent`. It's not wrong, just unrequested flexibility with its own test/story overhead for a state nothing in this codebase produces.
- `product-detail/index.tsx:1193` changes `onFindYourSizeClick` from opening the `'find-your-size'` tab to opening `'size-guide'` instead (the `'find-your-size'` tab itself, `index.tsx:907`, is untouched and still renders `comingSoon`). This is a real, if small, UX decision — "Find My Size" now silently shows Size Guide content — that SFCC-101 (which per your framing owns the Find My Size CTA) didn't ask this PR to make, and it isn't mentioned in the PR's own Summary, only buried in a commit message ("Find My Size falls back to Size Guide tab while Measmerize is unscoped"). Reasonable interim call, but it's a behaviour change riding uncalled-out in a ticket that's supposed to not need "any Measmerize-configured/not-configured branching."

Neither pulls in a new file owner, a new tier, or a different squad — both are contained inside files this PR was already touching for a legitimate reason, which is why I'm not calling them verdict-changing.

**3. Anything load-bearing missing?** Nothing named in the ticket. One thing worth naming that isn't a ticket-AC miss but is a real, verifiable code gap: `contentful.ts:331`'s comment on `measurementInstructions` still reads `/** Typed but not rendered — @contentful/rich-text-react-renderer not installed (Hard Rule #7). */` — but `sizeGuideContent.tsx:43` (`renderMeasurementInstructions`) and its call site at `:272` **do** render it now, just through a hand-rolled minimal renderer (paragraph nodes + bold/italic only). The comment is stale, not accurate. Combined with `sizeGuide.js`'s `RICH_TEXT_VALIDATIONS` (final state, lines 5-22) permitting headings, lists, quotes, embedded entries, and underline/code marks — a content editor who uses any of what the CMS visibly allows them to use, beyond a plain paragraph with bold/italic, will have that content silently vanish on the PDP with no error and no fallback. Not named in SFCC-102's text, so not a scope gap against the ticket — but a real content-editor trap, and the one comment that should explain the limitation instead asserts something false.

**4. The `mm`/`defaultUnit` inconsistency — acceptable, or a real gap?** Confirmed exactly as you found it: `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts:344` is `defaultUnit?: 'cm' | 'inch'` (mm genuinely dropped), while `scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuide.js:175` is `validations: [{ in: ['cm', 'inch', 'mm'] }]` (mm genuinely still permitted), with an explicit, reasoned comment two lines above it explaining why (matches the live Contentful dev schema; renderer treats anything non-cm/non-inch as cm; kept to avoid changing a live shared schema without sign-off). **On the code-behaviour axis this is fine** — it's inert, documented, and defensible, not a scope gap against SFCC-102 (the ticket never mentions `mm` either way).

**On the PR-accuracy axis it's a real problem, and it's worse than just this one line.** The PR body's "Required actions before merging" says the change "removes `mm` from `defaultUnit` validation" and the Test checklist has `[x] npm run install:contentful ... defaultUnit dropdown no longer shows mm` checked off. Both are false against the final diff — the commit history shows `mm` was removed (`4421c5fb`), then deliberately put back nine commits earlier than the PR's current head is misleading about (`eb7f32af`, "restore ... to match live Contentful dev schema; add 'mm' to defaultUnit allowed values"), and the PR body was never updated to match. This isn't a scope gap against SFCC-102 — it's a false claim in the exact section (`sizeGuide.js` is Tier 2, Integration/SI-Partner-owned) that's supposed to tell that owner what they're being asked to approve. Fix: update the PR body's Required Actions and Test checklist to say `mm` is intentionally retained, not removed, before the SI partner reviews it.

**5. Is wiring only Size Guide and leaving Find My Size alone correct scoping?** Yes, on the file/content axis — `find-your-size` (`index.tsx:907`) still renders `comingSoon`, unchanged, exactly matching the sibling-ticket split you described. My one caveat is the `onFindYourSizeClick` redirect covered in point 2 — it's a defensible interim choice, but it is SFCC-102 quietly making a UX call that's arguably SFCC-101's to make, and it isn't disclosed in the PR's own Summary.

## Manifest / tier check

All 19 changed files, checked against `frozenFiles.md`/`protectedFiles.md`/`CODEOWNERS` directly (not just the PR's own table):

- **No Tier 1 file touched** — confirmed by grepping all 19 paths against every Tier 1 pattern in `frozenFiles.md`; zero matches. Not blocked.
- **Registry churn** (`.claude/registry/{components,hooks,pages}.md`) — expected, not a finding.
- **Two Tier 2 files were modified but not disclosed in the PR's own "Changed files"/"Required actions" table**, despite one Tier 2 file (`sizeGuide.js`) in the same governance bucket being correctly flagged there: `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (routes to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-2-approvers` per `CODEOWNERS:117` — one mechanical line registering the new recipe, low risk) and `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` (routes to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-2-approvers` per `CODEOWNERS:146`, same "Contentful Schema Definitions" bucket as `sizeGuide.js` in `protectedFiles.md`). **This does not put anything at risk of merging unreviewed** — CODEOWNERS enforces the real reviewer gate server-side regardless of what the PR body says, per this repo's own stated philosophy that the PR text isn't the security boundary. What it does mean is the "notify Integration/SI Partner before changing" step — a human, pre-merge, live-Contentful-sandbox step that CODEOWNERS can't retroactively catch — was only visibly done for one of the two Tier 2 files this PR touches.
- `zimmTable.css.ts`, `useContentful.ts`, `sizeGuideContent.stories.tsx` — real Tier 4 files also missing from the PR's own table, but same owner/tier as their listed siblings; low materiality, just table hygiene.

## What Marcel is missing

The stale `contentful.ts:331` comment ("not rendered") sitting on a field that the same PR now actively renders, next to a CMS schema that still advertises headings/lists/quotes the renderer will silently swallow — that's a live trap for whoever next touches Contentful content for this entry, and nothing in the diff would warn them. Separately, worth registering: this PR was Claude-co-authored on every commit, and it's the one that under-applied AGENTS.md's own Tier 2 notify-before-changing rule to 2 of the 3 protected files it touched — that's a build-loop discipline signal, not just a one-PR fix.</result>

<result>## Test Coverage & React Logic Review — PR #113 (SFCC-102 Size Guide)

Scope: `useSizeGuide.ts`/`.test.ts`, `sizeGuideContent.tsx`/`.test.ts`/`.stories.tsx`, `zimmTable/index.tsx`/`.test.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`, `useContentful.ts`'s `enabled` param. Ran a scoped `npx vitest run` on all four test files from the worktree: **44/44 pass**, confirming the read findings below aren't masked by failing/skipped tests.

### Summary

The pure-logic layer (`convertCm`, `toDisplayRows`, `normaliseKey`, `useContentfulEntries`'s locale-reset/abort handling, `resolveLinkedAssets`) is well tested — DAMP names, real edge cases, good Arrange/Act/Assert. But the component-render layer has a real, confirmed hole: `SizeGuideContent` — the component carrying essentially all of this PR's branching logic — has **zero Vitest render coverage**, and the one Storybook `play` function that exists doesn't actually prove the feature it looks like it proves. This is not a nitpick about "should have more tests"; it's the exact pattern `testing.md`'s own opening section calls out as insufficient (relying on another surface to prove a component's own contract).

---

### Critical Gaps

**1. `SizeGuideContent` has no render-level test anywhere in the codebase — 🔴 8/10 — CONFIRMED — UNIFORM**
`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.test.ts` (all 72 lines) contains zero `render(` calls — confirmed both by reading the file and by grep. It only tests the two exported pure helpers. The component itself has real decision logic completely unexercised by Vitest: `isValidTable` gating per table (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:237-248`), the `hasTables` fallback-image gate (`:249`, `:334-351`), `hideHeading`/custom-`heading` override logic (`:279-287` and its two siblings), and `showToggle` gated on `hasConvertibleRows` (`:211-217`). `product-detail/index.tsx` (the only real call site, `:904`) also has no test file — `product-detail/` only has `variantScopedPrice.test.ts` and `productInfo.test.ts`, neither touching size guide. So the only thing that ever renders this component is Storybook, and only 1 of 8 stories (`Default`) has a `play` function. Per `testing.md`'s explicit guidance (and its own worked example, `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx`), a component with this much of its own branching needs its own test file with the child/hook mocked out — not reliance on a sibling story. This is the root cause of findings 2 and 4 below.

**2. Zero verification of `useContentful.ts`'s `enabled` param, from either side — 🔴 8/10 — CONFIRMED — UNIFORM**
`useContentful.test.ts` has 4 describe blocks (locale-change handling, `getValidatedContentfulConfig`, `buildContentfulUrl`, `resolveLinkedAssets`) — none exercise the 4th `enabled` argument; every `useContentfulEntries` call in the file is the 3-arg form (grep for `enabled` in that file: zero hits). So there's no test proving: `enabled=false` skips the fetch, `enabled=false` resets `data`/`error`/`isLoading` (`useContentful.ts:132-136`), or `false→true` triggers a fetch. Separately, `useSizeGuide.test.ts` mocks `useContentfulEntries` entirely and never inspects `mockEntries.mock.calls` (confirmed via grep — zero `toHaveBeenCalledWith`/`mock.calls` in that file), so the wiring `useSizeGuide.ts:40` (`!!sizeGuideKey` → `enabled`) is itself unverified. A regression that hardcodes `enabled=true` (silently defeating the "skip fetch for products without a size guide" optimization the code comments claim) would pass every existing test. Real-world failure mode: if the PDP component persists across client-side product navigation, a broken reset-on-disable could leak a previous product's size-guide tables onto a product that shouldn't have one — a content-correctness bug for a commerce page, not just a wasted API call.

**3. CM/INCH sibling-independence — the component's own documented headline behavior — has no verification anywhere — 🔴 7/10 — CONFIRMED — UNIFORM (consequence of #1)**
`ConvertibleTableSection`'s own JSDoc (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:194-197`) claims "Each instance's toggle only affects its own table, not sibling tables." Tracing the only assertion that touches this at all — the `Default` story's `play` (`sizeGuideContent.stories.tsx:174-186`) — its fixture (`SIZE_GUIDE_ENTRY`) has `sizeConversionsTable` rows all `convertible:false`, so that table's `hasConvertibleRows` is `false` and its toggle is suppressed entirely (`:217`). Only `bodyMeasurementsTable` ever renders a toggle in this fixture, meaning `canvas.getAllByRole('button', {name:/inch/i})` returns exactly **one** button. The assertion "size conversions cell `'2'` stays unchanged" therefore proves only that non-convertible *rows* don't get converted — it structurally cannot prove sibling *toggle state* independence, since there's no second toggle in the DOM to interfere. The one fixture with two simultaneously-toggleable tables (`Gloves`, `:213-219` — body + garment measurements, both convertible, `hasCmInchToggle:true`) has **no `play` function at all**. Net result: the signature feature this PR was built around has zero test evidence, direct or indirect.

---

### Important Improvements

**4. `useSizeGuide`'s 3-priority resolution — precedence between priority 1 and 2 is never actually tested, only presence — 🟡 6/10 — CONFIRMED — UNIFORM**
Read every test in `useSizeGuide — resolution priority` (`useSizeGuide.test.ts:31-98`). The priority-1 test (`:53-61`) fixture is `[defaultEntry, localeEntry]` — proves priority 1 beats priority 3, but has no priority-2 (`locales[]`-match) candidate present to compete against. The priority-2 test (`:63-70`) fixture is `[defaultEntry, localesEntry]` — correctly proves priority 2 beats priority 3 (both present together, as it should be). But no test ever puts a priority-1 candidate and a priority-2 candidate in the same `entries` array simultaneously, so "priority 1 beats priority 2" is asserted only by code inspection of the `??` chain (`useSizeGuide.ts:51-58`), never by a test that could catch a future reordering/rescoring regression. For an international retailer where the wrong regional size chart is a real user-facing harm, this precedence deserves an explicit test with both candidates co-present.

**5. `ZimmTable` never asserts the actual `colSpan` DOM attribute — only text presence — 🟡 7/10 — CONFIRMED — UNIFORM**
`columnSpan`/`subColumns`/`spans` exist solely to control `colSpan` (`index.tsx:88`, `:103`, `:169`, `:174`, `:215` etc.), and this is the entire distinguishing purpose of the grouped-header variants. `index.test.tsx` (all 82 lines, confirmed via grep for "colspan": zero hits) only ever asserts `getByText`/`getAllByText`/`querySelectorAll('th'|'td'|'tr').length`. A regression that always rendered `colSpan={1}` (fully breaking grouped headers/merged cells) would pass all 8 existing tests.

**6. Malformed-Contentful-data: `columns` array elements aren't type-checked — a real crash path, currently untested — 🟡 7/0 — PLAUSIBLE — ONE-OFF**
`isValidTable` (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:227-230`) checks `Array.isArray(t.columns)` but never validates element types. Per the function's own comment, Contentful's "Object" field type has zero structural validation, so an editor mistake can produce a non-string element. Traced: `columns.map((col,j) => <chakra.th>{col}</chakra.th>)` (`zimmTable/index.tsx:165-177`) — if `col` is an object, React throws "Objects are not valid as a React child," crashing the size-guide drawer render with no test covering it. By contrast, `row.label` being `undefined` (also unguarded by `isValidTable`) is traced to be harmless — React silently renders `undefined` as nothing, producing a blank label cell rather than a crash (🔵 3/10, untested but non-critical). `spans` not summing to `cells.length` was also traced to degrade gracefully (defaults to `colSpan=1`, at worst a visual misalignment, no crash).

**7. `ZimmTable`'s empty-`rows` case is tested only for the standard variant — 🔵 4/10 — CONFIRMED (traced, not a live bug) — ONE-OFF**
`'renders empty rows without crashing'` exists only in the "standard table" describe block (`index.test.tsx:34-37`). Traced the labelless+bordered branch with `rows=[]`: `Math.max(...[].map(...))` (`index.tsx:65`) evaluates `Math.max()` with no arguments → `-Infinity`, then `Array.from({length: -Infinity})` (`:69`) relies on the `ToLength` spec clamp (negative → `0`) to avoid a `RangeError`. It doesn't crash, but the safety is a JS-spec coincidence, not an explicit guard — worth a defensive test given how easily a refactor could break the assumption invisibly.

---

### Test Quality Issues

None found that are testing implementation over behavior — the existing suites (`useContentful.test.ts`'s locale-reset/abort tests in particular, and `useSizeGuide.test.ts`'s priority-3/normalisation tests) are genuinely well-designed, DAMP-named, and behavior-focused. The issues here are gaps, not brittleness.

---

### React Stateful-Logic Correctness — `ConvertibleTableSection`'s `useEffect`

`useEffect(() => setUnit(initialUnit), [initialUnit, table])` (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:207-209`) — traced the full reference chain rather than assuming:

- `sizeConversionsTable`/`bodyMeasurementsTable`/`garmentMeasurementsTable` (`:237-248`) are plain ternary property reads off `sizeGuide.fields` — not new object constructions — so they only change identity when `sizeGuide` itself changes identity.
- `sizeGuide` is `useSizeGuide`'s `useMemo` output (`useSizeGuide.ts:43-59`), deps `[entries, sizeGuideKey, locale]`. `entries` only gets a new array reference when `useContentfulEntries`'s fetch effect re-runs (`useContentful.ts:131-175`), gated by `[contentType, preview, locale, enabled]` — and the `locale` passed into *this specific* hook is the hardcoded `CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE` (`useSizeGuide.ts:39`), not the SFCC display locale, so it's stable post-mount.

**Verdict: PLAUSIBLE design smell, not a CONFIRMED live bug.** Given today's call chain, I could not construct a path where `table` gets a new-but-equal reference on an unrelated parent re-render — so a user's manual toggle should survive an unrelated re-render as things stand. But this correctness is *coincidental*, resting entirely on the one-shot-fetch chain rather than any explicit guarantee — neither `SizeGuideContent` nor `ConvertibleTableSection` is wrapped in `React.memo` (confirmed via grep, zero hits), so nothing structurally prevents a future change (e.g., a caching layer swap, or a refactor that constructs `sizeGuide` fresh per render) from silently reintroducing exactly the reset bug the task asked me to check for. Depending on object identity (`table`) for what is semantically a value-based reset condition is the kind of thing `testing.md` flags as needing a regression test precisely because it "would survive a refactor invisibly if broken" — and per finding #1, no such test exists (there's no render test of `SizeGuideContent`/`ConvertibleTableSection` at all to hang it on). I'd rate this 🟡 6/10 — real latent fragility, not an active bug. A cheap, targeted improvement: drop `table` from the dependency array (the comment/intent is "reset when the default changes," which `initialUnit` alone already captures) or add a fixture-level test that toggles, forces a re-render with unchanged props, and asserts the toggle didn't reset.

`useSizeGuide.ts`'s own `useMemo` deps (`:59`, `[entries, sizeGuideKey, locale]`) are correct and complete — exactly the three external values the callback reads. No stale-closure risk.

---

### Positive Observations

- `useContentful.test.ts`'s locale-change reset/abort-guard tests (`:59-118`) are excellent — they test the exact "superseded request can't clobber the current one" race condition with real controllable promises, not mocked timers.
- `useSizeGuide.test.ts`'s priority-3/normalisation/null-handling tests are precise and behavior-focused.
- `ZimmTable`'s three render-branch split is structurally tested at the surface level (headers render, `th`/`td` counts are right, spacer rows appear) — the gap is depth (attribute-level), not absence.
- `toDisplayRows`'s range-conversion and non-numeric-passthrough tests (`sizeGuideContent.test.ts:41-61`) cover genuinely tricky regex edge cases (en-dash vs hyphen) well.</result>

content.text: The conventions sub-review just landed with strong, well-cited findings (a DRY violation that reproduces a form-submit bug pattern already seen on other PRs, a discriminated-union gap corroborating what the scope reviewer found independently, token/magic-number nits). It also surfaced a locale regex detail that I chased down myself — and it's a real one: the Contentful schema's `key` field requires a full `xx_XX`-style locale suffix, but four of the eight storefronts (AU, and the French/Italian/Spanish EU sites) have bare single-part locale IDs (`en`, `fr`, `it`, `es`) with no region part. The locale-canonicalization fix that CodeRabbit flagged and the author marked fixed only converts hyphens to underscores — it never maps a bare locale to its region-qualified form, so it's currently impossible to ever author a working locale-specific size guide for the French, Italian, or Spanish storefronts specifically. Not visibly broken today only because no one's authored that content yet. Still waiting on the remaining four sub-reviews before I put together the full picture.

### Pre-check: is `role="group"` + `aria-label="Unit"` correct, not just present?

Per WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, `aria-labelledby` is preferred *only* when a visible label element already exists to point at (avoiding duplicated strings) — here there is none, so `aria-label` isn't just acceptable, it's the *only* mechanism available. So this is required, not optional, and correctly implemented. `aria-pressed={active}` on each `NavItem` (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:85`) correctly satisfies 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value for the toggle's state.

### F1 — Row-header cell is a `<td>`, not `<th scope="row">` (standard variant)

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTable/index.tsx:205-207`**
```tsx
<chakra.td __css={styles.labelTd} borderBottom={BORDER_SECONDARY}>
  {row.label}
</chakra.td>
```
Every row label in the standard variant ("Bust", "Waist", "Hips", "XS"/"S"/"M"/"L", "Small"/"Medium"/"Large" — see `sizeGuideContent.stories.tsx:20-23, 31-33, 93-96`) renders as a plain `<td>`. This isn't a missing-attribute problem — `<td>` is *never* eligible to be inferred as a header by the HTML5 header-association algorithm regardless of position, so no `scope` value could fix it short of changing the element itself to `<th>`. A screen reader user navigating cell-by-cell (e.g. JAWS/NVDA table navigation, which announces headers per cell) gets a value like "86" with zero programmatic link back to "Waist" or to the column ("M"). Compounding this, `labelTd`'s style (`zimmTable.css.ts:45-52`) uses the identical `textStyle: 'caption'` as regular `td` cells (`zimmTable.css.ts:38-42`) — no bold/weight distinction either, so even sighted users have only left-alignment as a "this is special" cue.
- WCAG: **1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A)**
- Severity: 🔴 must-fix
- CONFIRMED
- **UNIFORM** — this is the shared `ZimmTable` atom; every current and future standard-variant table (size conversions, body/garment measurements, jewellery, any future category) inherits this exact gap.

### F2 — No `scope` attribute anywhere in the file (complex multi-level headers)

Grepped the whole file for `scope=`: zero matches. This matters most for the two genuinely complex header structures pulled from real prop shapes in the stories file:
- **Gloves** (`sizeGuideContent.stories.tsx:62-70`): a 2-row `thead` — main columns "SHORT GLOVES"/"LONG GLOVES" each `colSpan=2` (`index.tsx:169,174`), with a second row of repeating "S/M"/"M/L" sub-column headers (`index.tsx:180-200`). Neither the group header nor the sub-headers carry `scope="colgroup"`/`scope="col"`.
- **Hats** (`sizeGuideContent.stories.tsx:112-124`): labelless+bordered mode where an `isHeader` row ("S/M", "M/L") is a group header for the value row directly beneath it (`index.tsx:82-96`), also with no `scope`.
For the Gloves case specifically, this is the textbook scenario WCAG's own H63 technique exists for — colSpan/rowSpan header structures are exactly where browsers' implicit header-inference algorithm becomes unreliable across AT/browser combinations, unlike a single simple header row (which the plain AU/US/UK/EU/IT table in `sizeGuideContent.stories.tsx:17-24` mostly gets right by implicit inference alone, lower risk). Read `NavItem` (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:76-107`) in full: the only styling is `sx={{ background: 'none', padding: 0, borderWidth: 0, cursor: 'pointer' }}` plus the `active`-driven underline (lines 92-96). There is no `_hover`, `_focusVisible`, `_active`, or `_disabled` anywhere, and it's a raw `chakra.button` (not Chakra's `<Button>`), so it does **not** pick up `zimmButton.css.ts`'s recipe at all — confirmed by `globalStyles.ts:351`'s own comment ("Buttons: none here — zimmButton.css.ts is the single source of truth, use Chakra's `<Button>`"), which this component doesn't use.

I checked for a global outline reset that would make this a real "invisible focus" failure: `globalStyles.ts:294`'s `outline: 'none'` is scoped to the `.zimm-form-control` class only (not applied here), and `_app/index.tsx:462`'s `outline: 0` is scoped to `SkipNavContent` only. **No blanket reset exists**, so `NavItem` falls back to the browser's native default focus outline — SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA) is technically satisfied, this is not a confirmed WCAG failure.

- CONFIRMED (no interactive-state styling exists; native fallback confirmed present, not stripped)
- ONE-OFF to this component's authoring choice, though the anti-pattern (raw `chakra.button` bypassing the registered recipe) is one other reviewers may find shareable

- `"|"` separator (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:121-123`): `color="var(--zimm-color-text-muted)"` (#969696) with `aria-hidden="true"`. I'm not raising this as a confirmed violation, but flagging it since it's a new token usage in this PR.
- Severity: 🔵 note (PLAUSIBLE, debatable applicability), no change needed to the parts I could verify as CONFIRMED CLEAN

**`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.tsx:345`**: `alt={fields?.label ?? ''}`. That's informational content, not decoration, so an empty alt would hide the entire drawer's content from AT users. Checked `contentful.ts:330`: `label: string` is typed as **required** (unlike its optional siblings `measurementInstructions?`, `sizeConversionsDescription?`, etc.), so by the type contract the `?? ''` fallback looks unreachable. But this file's own `isValidTable` guard (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:224-230`) explicitly documents that "Contentful's Object type has no structural validation" and defends against required-per-schema fields being absent in practice — the same risk applies to `label`. - WCAG: **1.1.1 Non-text Content (A)**
- Severity: 🟡 should-fix
- CONFIRMED the code path exists; PLAUSIBLE (not proven) that it fires on real data, given the required typing — but the codebase's own precedent argues against trusting that guarantee
- ONE-OFF (single fallback-image path)

### F6 — No programmatic name ties a `<table>` to its section heading

Checked all three `ZimmTable` render branches for `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, or `<caption>` on `<chakra.table>` — none exist, and `ZimmTableProps` (`index.tsx:15-38`) has no prop for one at all. The visible heading ("BODY MEASUREMENTS" etc.) is a separate `<chakra.h2>` in `TableSection` (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:138-141`) with no `id`, so even retrofitting `aria-labelledby` on the table isn't currently possible without also adding an id to the heading. A screen reader user jumping directly to a `<table>` via an elements/tables list (a common navigation shortcut) lands with no indication of which of up to three tables they're in — and this gets worse when `hideHeading` is set (`contentful.ts:322`, used by the Hats table), where there's no visible heading either.
- WCAG: **1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A)**
- Severity: 🟡 should-fix
- CONFIRMED
- **UNIFORM** — affects every `ZimmTable` instance, not just size guide.

**`index.tsx:76-79`**: the visual spacer row between Hats-style groups (`<chakra.tr><chakra.td __css={styles.spacerTd} colSpan={totalCols} /></chakra.tr>`) has no `aria-hidden`. - Severity: 🔵 note (best-practice, not a hard SC failure)
- CONFIRMED

`zimmTable/index.test.tsx` has zero accessibility-specific assertions (only counts of `th`/`td` elements and text presence) — it wouldn't catch F1 or F2 today. Flagging only because it affects which branch is practically live for a11y purposes; the dead-code angle itself belongs to the conventions lane.

No Figma file/node ID is referenced anywhere in this PR's diff or commit history for this ticket's size-guide/toggle work — every row below is unverifiable against a design source right now, which is itself worth flagging as an open question before sign-off.

| What to check | Figma node | Expected value | How to verify |

content.text: The contract-fidelity review just landed with the most significant finding of this whole review — and it corrects my own earlier version of it. I'd hand-reasoned that the Contentful key regex blocks bare locales (AU/France/Italy/Spain); this agent empirically tested the regex and found that's not actually where the break is. The real problem is the `locales` tag-array's allow-list: it was authored assuming every locale looks like `language_COUNTRY` without checking the actual regional config, so it lists five values (`en_FR`, `fr_FR`, `it_IT`, `es_ES`, `en_UK`) that match no real storefront, while missing the real ones. Net effect: 7 of this brand's 11 storefront/locale rows either can't get locale-specific content through any path the CMS's own on-screen help text would lead an editor to, or get silently forced to share one entry with a completely different storefront (UK and the EU-English site collide; US domestic and US international collide) with no way to tell them apart. One accessibility review still outstanding, then the build's own reconciliation pass.

Additionally, the data driving `spans`/`columnSpan` is Contentful-authored (`SizeGuideTable.spans`, `contentful.ts:292`) — there is no guarantee a future CMS entry keeps header/value colSpans perfectly aligned, which is a precondition the implicit algorithm depends on for even the fallback case to work.
- WCAG: **1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A)**
- Severity: 🔴 must-fix for the colSpan/rowSpan cases (Gloves, Hats); 🟡 should-fix for the simple single-header-row case as defense-in-depth
- CONFIRMED (verified by direct grep, exit code 1 / no matches)
- **UNIFORM** — same reasoning as F1; this is the shared atom.

### F3 — CM/INCH toggle has no styled interactive states; falls back to native focus (not a violation, but a real gap)

Read `NavItem` (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:76-107`) in full: the only styling is `sx={{ background: 'none', padding: 0, borderWidth: 0, cursor: 'pointer' }}` plus the `active`-driven underline (lines 92-96). There is no `_hover`, `_focusVisible`, `_active`, or `_disabled` anywhere, and it's a raw `chakra.button` (not Chakra's `<Button>`), so it does **not** pick up `zimmButton.css.ts`'s recipe at all — confirmed by `globalStyles.ts:351`'s own comment ("Buttons: none here — zimmButton.css.ts is the single source of truth, use Chakra's `<Button>`"), which this component doesn't use.

I checked for a global outline reset that would make this a real "invisible focus" failure: `globalStyles.ts:294`'s `outline: 'none'` is scoped to the `.zimm-form-control` class only (not applied here), and `_app/index.tsx:462`'s `outline: 0` is scoped to `SkipNavContent` only. **No blanket reset exists**, so `NavItem` falls back to the browser's native default focus outline — SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA) is technically satisfied, this is not a confirmed WCAG failure.

However, it is a real, avoidable inconsistency: the codebase has a ready-made `.zimm-focus-visible` utility class (`globalStyles.ts:318-323`) built exactly for this — `outline: var(--zimm-focus-ring)`, and `--zimm-focus-ring` (`zimmTokens.ts:68`) resolves to `border-width-default solid colors.border.focus` — **the literal same value** as `BORDER_FOCUS` in `zimmTable.css.ts:5`, which this same PR already uses decoratively elsewhere. So the "branded" focus ring exists and is one class away, but `NavItem` doesn't opt in, so keyboard users get an unbranded native ring instead of the house style used everywhere else.
- I searched the full commit history for these files (all 9 SFCC-102 commits) for a Figma node reference specific to the toggle's states: **no Figma node available to verify against** — no node ID or link appears anywhere in the diff or commit messages for this component's hover/focus/active treatment.
- Severity: 🟡 should-fix (design-system consistency, not a WCAG failure)
- CONFIRMED (no interactive-state styling exists; native fallback confirmed present, not stripped)
- ONE-OFF to this component's authoring choice, though the anti-pattern (raw `chakra.button` bypassing the registered recipe) is one other reviewers may find shareable

**Related note, worth Marcel's eye:** `NavItem`'s label colour (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:98-104`) is `var(--zimm-color-text-default)` **unconditionally** — it does not vary by `active` at all. Only the underline (lines 92-96) differs between active/inactive. This is WCAG-compliant (1.4.1 Use of Color isn't violated — state isn't conveyed by colour alone; the underline plus `aria-pressed` both do that job), but given the human reviewer's already-confirmed fix moved inactive-label colour from `text-muted` (2.95:1) to `text-default` to hit 4.5:1, it's worth double-checking this was the *intended* resolution — it also means active and inactive labels are now visually identical apart from the underline, which may or may not match Figma intent (see visual checkpoint table).

### F4 — Colour contrast: no new violation found beyond the already-fixed one

- `"|"` separator (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:121-123`): `color="var(--zimm-color-text-muted)"` (#969696) with `aria-hidden="true"`. Confirmed this is genuinely decorative — it conveys no information the "CM"/"INCH" text labels don't already convey, so it falls under 1.4.3's own "Incidental" exception (pure decoration). **CONFIRMED CLEAN.**
- Computed actual contrast from `colour.ts`/`zimmTokens.ts` values: `text-default` (#191919) on `bg-02` (ivory-200, #f6f4f1, the row-stripe colour) ≈ **16:1** — passes AA/AAA comfortably. `border-focus` (#191919, the active-underline/header-divider colour) against white/ivory is likewise far above the 3:1 needed for 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast. No issue.
- `border-secondary` (#d1d1d1, used for cell dividers/row bottom-borders) computes to only **≈1.53:1** against white — technically fails a 3:1 UI-boundary bar *if* 1.4.11 is judged to apply to table gridlines. This is genuinely debatable under WCAG's own scope for 1.4.11 (gridlines are typically considered supplementary once row/column position + header text already convey structure, and here the row-striping provides a redundant, higher-contrast grouping cue). I'm not raising this as a confirmed violation, but flagging it since it's a new token usage in this PR.
- Severity: 🔵 note (PLAUSIBLE, debatable applicability), no change needed to the parts I could verify as CONFIRMED CLEAN

### F5 — Fallback image `alt` can be empty string for genuinely informational content

**`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/sizeGuideContent.tsx:345`**: `alt={fields?.label ?? ''}`. This image only renders when `!hasTables` (line 334) — i.e., it *is* the entire size guide for that product category (see `SIZE_GUIDE_IMAGE_ONLY` story, `sizeGuideContent.stories.tsx:128-148`, where it's literally a size chart). That's informational content, not decoration, so an empty alt would hide the entire drawer's content from AT users. Checked `contentful.ts:330`: `label: string` is typed as **required** (unlike its optional siblings `measurementInstructions?`, `sizeConversionsDescription?`, etc.), so by the type contract the `?? ''` fallback looks unreachable. But this file's own `isValidTable` guard (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:224-230`) explicitly documents that "Contentful's Object type has no structural validation" and defends against required-per-schema fields being absent in practice — the same risk applies to `label`. Also worth noting: even the happy path uses the *entry's* label (e.g. "Accessories Size Guide") rather than the more specific `fields.image.fields.title` (Contentful's own asset-description field, e.g. "Size guide chart" per the story fixture) — not wrong, but a missed opportunity for a more descriptive alt.
- WCAG: **1.1.1 Non-text Content (A)**
- Severity: 🟡 should-fix
- CONFIRMED the code path exists; PLAUSIBLE (not proven) that it fires on real data, given the required typing — but the codebase's own precedent argues against trusting that guarantee
- ONE-OFF (single fallback-image path)

### F6 — No programmatic name ties a `<table>` to its section heading

Checked all three `ZimmTable` render branches for `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, or `<caption>` on `<chakra.table>` — none exist, and `ZimmTableProps` (`index.tsx:15-38`) has no prop for one at all. The visible heading ("BODY MEASUREMENTS" etc.) is a separate `<chakra.h2>` in `TableSection` (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:138-141`) with no `id`, so even retrofitting `aria-labelledby` on the table isn't currently possible without also adding an id to the heading. A screen reader user jumping directly to a `<table>` via an elements/tables list (a common navigation shortcut) lands with no indication of which of up to three tables they're in — and this gets worse when `hideHeading` is set (`contentful.ts:322`, used by the Hats table), where there's no visible heading either.
- WCAG: **1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A)**
- Severity: 🟡 should-fix
- CONFIRMED
- **UNIFORM** — affects every `ZimmTable` instance, not just size guide.

### F7 — Spacer row between groups is exposed to assistive tech (minor, additive finding)

**`index.tsx:76-79`**: the visual spacer row between Hats-style groups (`<chakra.tr><chakra.td __css={styles.spacerTd} colSpan={totalCols} /></chakra.tr>`) has no `aria-hidden`. It's purely a layout gap (`height`, `padding: 0`, per `zimmTable.css.ts:55-59`) with no data, but it's still a real, empty `<tr>`/`<td>` in the accessibility tree — a screen reader navigating row-by-row hits a meaningless blank row between the Hats table's OSFA/S-M-L groups.
- Severity: 🔵 note (best-practice, not a hard SC failure)
- CONFIRMED
- UNIFORM to the bordered+labelless variant specifically

### Context, not a separate finding
`zimmTable/index.test.tsx` has zero accessibility-specific assertions (only counts of `th`/`td` elements and text presence) — it wouldn't catch F1 or F2 today. Also, `ZimmTable` is only ever invoked via `ScrollableTable` (`sizeGuideContent.tsx:182-189`), which always sets `bordered={table.labelless}` — meaning the `labelless && !bordered` branch (`index.tsx:121-159`) is currently unreachable from any real caller (only exercised directly by the Vitest file). Flagging only because it affects which branch is practically live for a11y purposes; the dead-code angle itself belongs to the conventions lane.

---

### Visual checkpoint table (manual verification in a real browser)

No Figma file/node ID is referenced anywhere in this PR's diff or commit history for this ticket's size-guide/toggle work — every row below is unverifiable against a design source right now, which is itself worth flagging as an open question before sign-off.

## Gate table — head vs base (`develop`@ece4fc5d → head@5320652)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | Clean both sides |
| `npm test` | 1219/1219 passed, 83 files — I re-ran it myself, matches the CI bot exactly |
| `npm run lint` | 2 **new** prettier errors in `sizeGuideContent.tsx` (lines 98, 238) — contradicts the PR's own "0 errors" claim, auto-fixable |
| `audit:tokens` | 3 violations on both base and head, same files, none touched by this PR — pure inherited debt, not this PR's problem |
| Merge state | **CONFLICTING** against develop — but only in the 3 auto-generated registry files (timestamps/counts), trivial rebase + regen |
| Playwright/BrowserStack | Skipped — consistent with the change-scoped skip logic, didn't trace the exact reason |

## The five things that actually matter

**1. Content authors can't build most of the locale-specific size guides this feature is supposedly ready for.** [sizeGuide.js:142](scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuide.js:142) vs [useSizeGuide.ts:48-54](overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.ts:48). The Contentful `locales` tag field only accepts a fixed list of values, and whoever wrote that list assumed every storefront's locale looks like `language_COUNTRY` (e.g. `en_AU`) without checking the real config. Four real storefronts — UK, the English-language EU site, French, Italian, Spanish, US domestic, US international (7 of 11 storefront rows total) — either can't be given locale-specific content at all through any path the tool's own help text points an editor to, or get silently merged with a completely different storefront's guide with no way to tell them apart. This isn't theoretical: the on-screen field help text literally tells an editor to type in values (`fr_FR`, `en_UK`, etc.) that will never match anything a real shopper's browser produces. (My first pass at this got the mechanism wrong — I thought a regex blocked it; a deeper pass tested the regex directly and found the real fault is the allow-list. Corrected version above.)

**2 & 3. The size tables aren't readable by screen readers the way the schema requires.** [zimmTable/index.tsx:205-207](overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTable/index.tsx:205) uses a plain cell for row labels ("Bust", "Waist") instead of a proper header cell, so a screen reader announcing a value like "86" has no idea it's a bust measurement. And nowhere in the file is there a `scope` attribute, which matters most for the Gloves/Hats tables' two-level grouped headers — exactly the layout where a browser's own guesswork about which header belongs to which cell breaks down. Both live in the shared `ZimmTable` atom, so it's one fix that covers every size guide, current and future.

**4. An editor using a heading, list, link, or underline in "Measurement Instructions" will lose that content silently.** CodeRabbit caught this once, the author fixed it correctly (commit `b73a3e2`), and a later commit whose stated purpose was "sync to Contentful dev" undid the fix as a side effect — nobody, including CodeRabbit's own follow-up passes, noticed. The schema still allows all that formatting; the renderer still only understands plain paragraphs with bold/italic. There's also a comment on this exact field ([contentful.ts:331](overrides/app/types/contentful.ts:331)) that says it "isn't rendered" — which this same PR makes false.

**5. The PR's own headline feature — independent CM/INCH toggles per table — has no test that can prove it works, and the component holding all the logic has no test file at all.** Traced this precisely: the only story with two simultaneously-active toggles has no `play` assertion, and the one story that does have an assertion only ever has one toggle in the DOM to begin with, so it structurally cannot catch a regression where toggling one table's units affects another.

## Everything else (confirmed, lower stakes)

- `useSizeGuide` swallows fetch errors — a Contentful outage looks identical to "no size guide for this product," fails silently ([useSizeGuide.ts:35-59](overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.ts:35))
- PR body says `mm` was removed from both files; it was only removed from the TypeScript type — the Contentful schema deliberately kept it (good reason, just needs the PR text corrected before the Tier-2 reviewer reads it)
- Two Tier 2 files (`theme/components/index.ts`, `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js`) aren't in the PR's own disclosure tables, though a third Tier 2 file in the same PR is — process gap, not a merge-safety gap (CODEOWNERS gates it regardless)
- No test protects the `enabled`/fetch-gating fix, the locale-priority ordering, or `colSpan` (a regression collapsing every grouped header would pass all 8 tests)
- No table has a name tying it to its own heading — worse on the Hats table, which has no visible heading either
- A hand-rolled toggle button duplicates an existing shared atom and, in doing so, drops `type="button"` — same recurring shared-atom gap I've flagged on other PRs
- ~10 smaller nitpicks (magic numbers, an uncommented type cast, a primitive token where a semantic alias exists, an unreachable component branch) — full list in the findings file, not worth individual comments

**Confirmed clean, worth knowing so it's not re-litigated:** no XSS surface anywhere, no secrets, the `enabled` param change doesn't break any existing caller, the toggle's contrast fix is deliberate and already correct, and the scope itself is right — all three table types work end-to-end, and correctly leaves the Measmerize widget to its own separate ticket.

**Scope verdict: correctly scoped.** Nothing missing, two very minor over-scope items that don't change that.

content.text:
**80px vs 64px — resolved, and it's neither.** I pulled the actual Figma frame measurements (Body Measurements table, a real instanced frame, not a text node): the label column is **96px**, and each data column is **71px**. Kiera's "64px minimum" comment reads as a floor below that natural 71px for narrow viewports — not the target width itself. The code's `MIN_COL_WIDTH` (80px) matches none of these three numbers, and it's applied uniformly to both the label column and data columns, where Figma clearly authors them at two different widths (96 vs 71). Net effect: on a viewport where 6 columns at their natural 71px width would fit fine, the code forces every column to 80px minimum — wider than designed, which means the table pushes into horizontal-scroll mode earlier than Figma intends. This is a real, measured design-fidelity gap, not a null result.

Now, more depth on the four 🔴s and the test gap, since that's what the verdict hinges on:

**Locale allow-list (the big one).** Reproduction: an editor for the France storefront opens Contentful, creates a new size guide entry, and follows the field's own help text — which says to tag it `fr_FR`. They ship it. A French shopper never sees it; the storefront silently shows the generic default guide instead, forever, with nothing in any log or UI to say why. This isn't a "someday" bug — it's not reachable to fix by content authoring at all today, because the tool actively tells editors to use values that don't work. Blast radius: content correctness for France, Italy, Spain, UK, and both US storefronts (7 of 11 storefront/locale rows) — not a crash, not visible to a developer, only visible as "why doesn't the French size guide show up" weeks from now. This is a schema/data-model fix (the `locales` allow-list), not a code-logic fix — small diff, but someone has to actually decide the correct list against `regional.md` first.

**Accessibility (the two `<td>`/`scope` findings).** These aren't edge cases — every size guide table a screen reader user encounters, on any product, has this gap. A screen reader user tabbing through the size conversions table hears "8", "2P", "38P" as bare values with no indication of which row or column they belong to. This is a WCAG 2.2 AA violation (the project's own stated target), in a shared atom, so it compounds across every category (clothing, shoes, gloves, hats, belts) as more content gets authored. Fix is mechanical (swap `<td>` for `<th scope="row">`, add `scope` to the grouped headers) — genuinely small, not architecturally risky.

**Rich text validation regression.** Concrete failure: a content editor writes "Measurement Instructions" with a bulleted list or a link (both allowed by the schema today), publishes it, and it renders as nothing — the whole field silently disappears from the PDP. This already happened once in this PR's own history (fixed, then un-fixed by an unrelated commit) — which is itself worth noting to the author, since it's evidence the "sync to Contentful dev" commit wasn't reviewed carefully enough to catch what it was undoing.

**Test coverage on the toggle.** This one's lower stakes by itself — it's not a live bug, it's a hole. Nothing is confirmed broken; what's confirmed is that if someone breaks the per-table toggle independence in a refactor next month, nothing will catch it, and the one story that looks like it proves this can't. I'd weight this behind the other three for a "must fix before merge" call, more of a "before this component gets touched again" item.

None of the four require an architectural rework — they're each contained, mechanical fixes. The open question is really whether they're worth a merge-blocking round-trip now versus fast-follow tickets, given the PR is otherwise clean (scope, tests elsewhere, security, no regressions on develop). Where do you want to land?
